title: Lord of the stars
caption: The giant elliptical galaxy M87, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Messier 87, NGC 4486 · constellation Virgo · about 55 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)Acknowledgment: P. Cote (Herzberg Institute of Astrophysics) and E. Baltz (Stanford University)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Amid a smooth yellow glow of older stars, a soft blue jet and a swarm of star-like globular clusters stand out in this Hubble image. The galaxy is M87, a huge elliptical in Virgo, a constellation of the spring sky, some 54 million light-years from the Sun, home to several trillion stars, a supermassive black hole and some 13,000 globular clusters.

The jet is a stream of material driven by the black hole and flung out from the galaxy's core. As gas from the center falls onto the black hole, the energy set free powers a fire-hose jet of subatomic particles, accelerated to nearly the speed of light.

M87 dominates the heart of the Virgo Cluster, which holds some 2,000 galaxies, and it measures 120,000 light-years across. From that central position it may have gathered some of its globular clusters by pulling them away from nearby dwarf galaxies, which now seem to have none of their own.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.21 x 3.17 arcminutes) and distance (55 million light years), the frame spans roughly 51,000 × 51,000 light-years. Its light set out about 55 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed in blue, visible and near-infrared light. The color mapping isn't published, though older stars appear yellow and the jet blue.
understand.eye: Long exposures and near-infrared light reveal faint clusters beyond the reach of the eye.
